summary: Two concurrent-map method docs incorrectly promise atomic Java default-method behavior; several return-value docs also miss required tags.

items.issue: Claims that `ConcurrentMap.computeIfAbsent` is atomic “per the ConcurrentMap contract”. That contract does not guarantee atomicity for its default method; an arbitrary wrapped `ConcurrentMap` may use it. The implementation simply delegates to that method.
items.suggestion: Remove the atomicity claim and state that concurrency semantics are those of the wrapped map's `computeIfAbsent` implementation.

items.issue: Claims that `ConcurrentMap.compute` is atomic “per the ConcurrentMap contract”, but the contract does not guarantee atomicity for the default method used by arbitrary `ConcurrentMap` implementations.
items.suggestion: Remove the atomicity claim and document delegation to the wrapped map's `compute`, with its implementation-defined concurrency guarantees.
